readout_other: Auditory brainstem responses; auditory cortex LFP and MUA; skull acoustic emission sensor; FEM simulation of skull vibration
direction_notes: Cortical LFP responses in auditory cortex were evoked by TUS versus sham for all tapering window rates, while ABRs were absent or reduced with tapering of 3% (1 ms) or 15% (0.05 ms) and above.

exposures.label: Tapered-envelope TUS of auditory cortex, 0.05 or 1 ms bursts

timing.protocol_description: Single CW tone burst of 0.05 or 1 ms with cosine rise/fall tapering window rate h of 0-45% of burst duration. For ABRs, 500 trials per condition; PRF 5 Hz or 1 kHz tested with 0.05 ms bursts. LFP trials repeated 30 times.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Accordingly, our stimulation patterns of the CWs were generated by multiplying a sinusoidal signal (frequency, $f _ { \mathrm { c } } = 0 . 5$ MHz; angular velocity, $\omega _ { \mathrm { c } } = 2 \pi f _ { \mathrm { c } } )$ as a carrier wave by a window (tapering) function at the onset and offset of the stimulus (Fig. 1(a)).
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.pressure: Although we tested three acoustic pressure conditions–38, 79, 129 kPa–measured at 8 mm from the waveguide surface (Fig. 3(c)), we primarily focused on the responses to the 38-kPa condition since it represented the lowest level that consistently evoke the cortical responses.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: For the experiments involving US stimulation, the duration of the stimuli was either 0.05 or 1 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: A US transducer (V301-SU, Olympus, USA) was attached to a custom-made waveguide produced using a 3-D printer (Dreamer, FLASH-FORGE Co., Zhejiang, China).
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: A US transducer (V301-SU, Olympus, USA) was attached to a custom-made waveguide produced using a 3-D printer (Dreamer, FLASH-FORGE Co., Zhejiang, China).
source_quotes.n_subjects: We used nine male and six female C57BL/6J mice (Japan SLC, Japan; 6–13 weeks old) in the study.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: Thus, it is expected the acoustic pressure was 38 kPa in the recorded area (Fig. 3(c) and (d)).

flags.reason: Text says nine male and six female mice; total not stated as a number and not summed here. ABR n = 6, LFP n = 3 animals.

Recorded as the burst durations 0.05 ms and 1 ms converted to seconds.
